2608.21325.title: Move by Move: Measuring and Steering How LLMs Conduct Psychotherapy
2608.21325.paper_summary: Users increasingly turn to large language models for emotional support, yet little is known about how these models actually conduct a psychotherapy interaction. We introduce an ontology of ten therapeutic moves: compact, function-based categories grounded in the MULTI-60 inventory, validated through an annotation campaign with five licensed psychologists, and scaled with a judge-based approach that matches expert agreement. Applying it to real counseling transcripts and model-led sessions, we compare the move distributions between human clinicians and a panel of frontier models. Models over-use inquiry at up to three times the human rate, neglect psychoeducation, and are strongly context-anchored: they carry forward strategies initiated by a human clinician but rarely initiate them themselves. Exposing the ontology as a set of tools roughly halves the mean deviation from the human move distribution and improves turn-level alignment with human therapist by 7-9 percentage points, without any fine-tuning.
2608.21325.paper_summary_zh: 使用者越來越多地依賴大型語言模型來獲得情感支持，但對於這些模型實際上如何進行心理治療互動的了解仍然有限。<lb/>我們介紹了一個包含十種治療行為的本體論：這些行為是基於MULTI-60清單的緊湊功能性分類，通過與五位持牌心理學家的標註活動進行驗證，並通過匹配專家一致性的評判基礎方法進行擴展。<lb/>將其應用於真實的諮詢記錄和模型主導的會話，我們比較了人類臨床醫生與前沿模型小組之間的行為分佈。<lb/>模型在詢問方面的使用率高達人類的三倍，忽視心理教育，並且強烈依賴於上下文：它們延續了人類臨床醫生所啟動的策略，但很少自行啟動這些策略。<lb/>將本體論作為一組工具暴露出來，大約將人類行為分佈的平均偏差減半，並在不進行任何微調的情況下，將與人類治療師的回合級對齊提高了7-9個百分點。
